findings.summary: review-lenses.sh routes this diff to the 'documentation consistency / No code changed, do NOT review for code defects' lens, but docker-compose.test.yml is executable test infrastructure (pinned image digest, port binding, healthcheck command, mem_limit) whose correctness is functional, not prose -- the same class of gap the backlog already names for .yml files in M0.20/M0.28.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit that breaks the fixture (e.g. a healthcheck command not present in the image, a dropped mem_limit, or a tag substituted for the digest) would be reviewed under guidance telling the reviewer not to check for defects, so a broken fixture could be waved through as documentation. Verified independently this instance is correct: pulled the pinned digest, ran the compose file, confirmed cgroup mem_limit=268435456 bytes, confirmed '0:9000' bound to a random host port, and confirmed the healthcheck reached 'healthy' in correlation with the S3 API answering 200 on /minio/health/live -- so no action needed on this file today, this is a gate-design observation only.

notes: No test code (JUnit/T0-T4) is present in this diff -- only a Docker Compose fixture definition and a one-line backlog status flip (todo -> done); FR-8 in the Serves column is unchanged in both hunks. The prompt that launched this review described a prior disagreement about the Serves column changing between FR-8 and '--', and asked me to arbitrate it; that edit is not present anywhere in the actual staged diff (only the State column changed), so there is nothing to arbitrate and no verdict is recorded on it here. The fixture being unconsumed by any test is expected: the same backlog row explicitly re-scopes the conformance suite to M1 because it depends on the BinStore SPI (M1.1), so the fixture is deliberately orphaned pending that milestone, not a gap in this commit.
